topics.label: Welcome and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and sets the clinical and biological scope of the course.

topics.label: Biological origins, differentiation failure, and tissue architecture in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They explain cancer as a disease arising from accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue structure.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumors through invasion, progression, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: They characterize benign and malignant neoplasms by evaluating their capacity for tissue invasion, histological progression from precursor lesions, and standard naming conventions.

topics.label: Mechanisms of tumor-induced illness, mortality, and comparative cancer incidence
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the physiological mechanisms by which tumors cause disease and death while surveying cancer incidence patterns across human tissues and diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical rationale, methods, and limitations of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the clinical justification for early cancer detection and compare the approaches and diagnostic efficacy of screening for different tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practicals preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by directing students to review the learning outcomes and preparing them for upcoming practical sessions.
